hunks.baseline: Returning to everyday life usually means stability.
hunks.sol: Returning to everyday life usually means things have settled down.

hunks.baseline: But immediately after the mysterious death of Siegfried Wassmann, we returned to our respective positions only to face a frantic stretch of time.
hunks.sol: But after Siegfried Wassmann’s mysterious death, we went back to our respective posts only to find ourselves busier than ever.

hunks.baseline: “The magical-power distribution in the C-rank Gate in Sokcho, Gangwon Province, is rising rapidly. It’s currently at Stage Two…… entering Stage Three! It’s a mutation Gate!”
hunks.sol: “The magical-power reading at the C-rank Gate in Sokcho, Gangwon Province, is rising rapidly. It’s at Stage Two… entering Stage Three! We have a mutation Gate!”

hunks.baseline: “How many people can we deploy right now?”
hunks.sol: “How many people can we deploy?”

hunks.baseline: “Four teams are on standby at the Gangwon Province branch. If we use the Teleport Magic circle connected to Sokcho City Hall, they can be sent to the site within five minutes.”
hunks.sol: “Four teams are on standby at the Gangwon Province branch. The Teleport Magic Formation linked to Sokcho City Hall can get them to the site within five minutes.”

hunks.baseline: “Send them out immediately. This could lead to a monster wave if we’re not careful, so make rescuing survivors and quickly suppressing the situation our top priorities.”
hunks.sol: “Send them now. This could turn into a monster wave. Make rescuing survivors and containing the situation your top priorities.”

hunks.baseline: The situation after our return was, quite literally, the worst.
hunks.sol: The situation after our return was about as bad as it could get.

hunks.baseline: Until only a few years ago, mutation Gates had occurred no more than once a month. Now, three or four were appearing every day—and that figure was limited to Korea alone.
hunks.sol: Until a few years ago, mutation Gates had appeared no more than once a month. Now we were seeing three or four a day—and that was just in Korea.

hunks.baseline: Instead of stock prices, the magical-power distribution chart was hitting an upward trend every single day without fail.
hunks.sol: While stock prices rose and fell, magical-power readings climbed every single day.

hunks.baseline: Every broadcasting station cut back on entertainment programming, while the newly established disaster-breaking-news channels featured experts from every field engaging in fierce debates.
hunks.sol: Broadcasters cut back on entertainment shows. On newly launched disaster-news channels, experts from every field argued fiercely.

hunks.baseline: “Many people overlook the fact that the rise in magical-power distribution has been happening steadily every year. Compared to the period immediately after the Great Cataclysm, the current figure is actually on the low side. Once this situation is over, things will calm down quickly, so there’s no need for the public to worry—”
hunks.sol: “Many people overlook the fact that magical-power readings have risen steadily every year. Compared to the period immediately after the Great Cataclysm, today’s readings are actually quite low. Once this situation is resolved, things will settle down quickly, so the public needn’t worry—”

hunks.baseline: “Calm down quickly? What kind of nonsense is that? And how can you compare things to immediately after the Great Cataclysm? To put it bluntly, after we killed the Demon King on the ‘Day of Victory,’ did humanity put down its weapons and all dance Ganggangsullae together?[^1] Back then, you could go to Han River Park and see lizardmen. Do you not remember that it took nearly a year just to deal with the monster armies that remained?”
hunks.sol: “Settle down quickly? What kind of nonsense is that? And how can you compare today with the period right after the Great Cataclysm? After we killed the Demon King on the ‘Day of Victory,’ did humanity put down its weapons and dance Ganggangsullae together?[^1] Back then, you could go to Han River Park and find lizardmen. It took nearly a year just to finish off the monster armies that were still out there. Have you forgotten?”

hunks.baseline: “I live in Ilsan, so I never saw lizardmen in Han River Park. I’m right.”
hunks.sol: “I live in Ilsan, and I never saw any lizardmen in Han River Park. I’m right.”

hunks.baseline: “What a fucking moron…”
hunks.sol: “What a fucking idiot…”

hunks.baseline: “Come on, now. You’re a year younger than me, so watch your language.”
hunks.sol: “Now, now. You’re a year younger than me. No need to swear.”

hunks.baseline: “A year younger, my ass, you fucking bastard. My parents filed my birth registration late. Happy now?”
hunks.sol: “A year younger, my ass, you fucking bastard. My parents registered my birth late. Happy?”

hunks.baseline: “Mr. Host, are you really going to sit there and watch this?”
hunks.sol: “Mr. Host, are you going to let him talk to me like that?”

hunks.baseline: It was no longer particularly surprising to see silver-haired authorities in academia turn red in the face on television and engage in title matches over their respective arguments.
hunks.sol: The sight of white-haired academic authorities turning red in the face on TV and fighting over whose argument would win was no longer particularly surprising.

hunks.baseline: Even as they grabbed one another by the collars, the news on the next channel was reporting breaking developments about mutation Gates or monster waves somewhere in the world.
hunks.sol: While they grabbed each other by the collars, the next channel was reporting breaking news of a mutation Gate or monster wave somewhere in the world.

hunks.baseline: And in the middle of those horrific scenes, I did my best to struggle through them.
hunks.sol: And at those horrific scenes, I fought as hard as I could.

hunks.baseline: The spearhead of White Flame smoothly cut through leather and bone harder than armor.
hunks.sol: White Flame’s spearhead sliced cleanly through hide and bone harder than armor.

hunks.baseline: The enormous monster—I had no idea how many I’d killed by then—stopped dead in its tracks. Then it slowly turned around and split in two from top to bottom.
hunks.sol: The enormous monster—I’d lost count of how many I’d killed—stopped dead. It slowly turned toward me and split down the middle.

hunks.baseline: The moment its three-meter-tall body fell, divided into two perfectly equal halves, I locked eyes with a man who had fallen a few steps away.
hunks.sol: As its three-meter body fell in two equal halves, I met the eyes of a man sprawled a few steps away.

hunks.baseline: He had survived by the narrowest margin, and in his hand was a plastic picket sign with red-painted letters.
hunks.sol: He had escaped death by a hair. In his hand was a plastic protest sign painted with red letters.

hunks.baseline: I wondered how I was supposed to react in a situation like this, then simply gave him a bitter smile.
hunks.sol: I wondered how I was supposed to react, then gave him a rueful smile.

hunks.baseline: Even if he hated me that much, using three exclamation marks was going a little too far.
hunks.sol: Even if he hated me, three exclamation marks seemed a bit much.

hunks.baseline: “You look fine apart from a few scratches, but stay seated just in case. It’s all over anyway, so the rescue team will be here soon.”
hunks.sol: “You look all right apart from a few scratches, but stay seated just in case. It’s over now. The rescue team will be here soon.”

hunks.baseline: I turned away from the man, who was only moving his lips.
hunks.sol: I left the man moving his lips without a word and turned away.

hunks.baseline: In the street, reduced to a wasteland in barely thirty minutes, the corpses of dead monsters were mixed together with human bodies.
hunks.sol: In barely thirty minutes, the street had been devastated. Monster carcasses lay among human bodies.

hunks.baseline: I sharpened my senses and searched the surroundings, but I could no longer feel any signs of life.
hunks.sol: I sharpened my senses and searched the area, but felt no other signs of life.

hunks.baseline: *It wasn’t supposed to cause this much damage.*
hunks.sol: *The damage never should have been this bad.*

hunks.baseline: It was a tragedy that a monster wave had occurred in this peaceful little city.
hunks.sol: It was tragic enough that a monster wave had struck this peaceful little city.

hunks.baseline: And it was also a tragedy that the hundreds of protesters who had gathered to condemn me had chosen this street as their rallying point.
hunks.sol: And that the hundreds of protesters gathered to condemn me had chosen this street for their rally.

hunks.baseline: I crossed the street, stepping through puddles where red and blue blood had mixed together.
hunks.sol: I crossed the street through puddles of mingled red and blue blood.

hunks.baseline: Hyenas that had gathered after catching the scent wasted no time rushing in with cameras and microphones.
hunks.sol: The hyenas had already caught the scent. They rushed me with cameras and microphones.

hunks.baseline: “What do you think about this monster wave?”
hunks.sol: “What do you think of this monster wave?”

hunks.baseline: “You arrived faster than anyone else and suppressed the monster wave! First of all, as a fellow human being, I’d like to express my deepest gratitude—”
hunks.sol: “You arrived before anyone else and stopped the monster wave! First, as a fellow human being, I’d like to express my deepest gratitude—”

hunks.baseline: “These people had gathered to condemn you. Is it possible that this monster wave was artificially caused by someone who supports you—”
hunks.sol: “These people were here to condemn you. Could someone who supports you have caused this monster wave deliberately—”

hunks.baseline: “Why has Mr. Sky still not shown himself? What connection do you have to the death of Siegfried Wassmann, who died recently?”
hunks.sol: “Why hasn’t Mr. Sky appeared yet? What connection do you have to the recent death of Siegfried Wassmann?”

hunks.baseline: It felt as though filth were pouring down on me from every direction.
hunks.sol: It felt as though filth were raining down on me from every direction.

hunks.baseline: There were people defending me, but far more reporters were frantic to come up with sensational headlines.
hunks.sol: A few defended me, but far more reporters were desperate for sensational headlines.

hunks.baseline: And many of them had probably been paid a considerable amount of money by someone else in exchange for asking questions like these.
hunks.sol: And I suspected many of them were being paid handsomely to ask those questions.

hunks.baseline: For example…
hunks.sol: By someone like…

hunks.baseline: *The Odin Guild.*
hunks.sol: *Odin Guild.*

hunks.baseline: It was something I had already more or less expected. Even when Team Leader Choi first told me about it, I hadn’t been particularly surprised.
hunks.sol: I’d already suspected as much. I hadn’t been particularly surprised when Team Leader Choi first told me.

hunks.baseline: Worsening public opinion through media control.
hunks.sol: Turn the media against us, and public opinion would follow.

hunks.baseline: Blatantly dragging me and the Ares Guild, which enjoyed overwhelming public support, through the mud was not something just anyone could attempt.
hunks.sol: Dragging me and Ares Guild through the mud so openly, when we had overwhelming public support, wasn’t something just anyone could attempt.

hunks.baseline: But Michael Silbert had enough power and justification to do exactly that.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert had both the power and the justification to try.

hunks.baseline: The problem was that, at least where the media was concerned, his efforts were working far better than I had imagined.
hunks.sol: The problem was that, in the media at least, it was working far better than I’d imagined.

hunks.baseline: “The Prophet still hasn’t revealed himself. What would you like to say to The Prophet, who is surely watching you from somewhere?”
hunks.sol: “The Prophet still hasn’t shown himself. What would you say to him, knowing he’s watching you from somewhere?”

hunks.baseline: “Statistics show that while the Ares Guild suppresses an average of 3.6 incidents per day, the Odin Guild resolves 6.5. Do you have anything to say about that?”
hunks.sol: “Statistics show that Ares Guild handles an average of 3.6 incidents a day, while Odin Guild handles 6.5. Any comment?”

hunks.baseline: “Hey, you! What kind of question is that? Do you call yourselves reporters?”
hunks.sol: “Hey, you! What kind of question is that? You call yourselves reporters?”

hunks.baseline: “Everyone, move back. Now!”
hunks.sol: “Everyone, step back. Now!”

hunks.baseline: It was pure chaos.
hunks.sol: It was chaos.

hunks.baseline: Reporters rushing forward in pursuit of more articles and payment. Police officers and Hunters trying to hold those reporters back.
hunks.sol: Reporters pushed forward for more stories and more payoffs. Police officers and Hunters struggled to hold them back.

hunks.baseline: I slipped through them, feeling as though my insides were twisting, while listening to someone’s voice echoing in my head.
hunks.sol: I slipped between them, my stomach churning, while a voice seemed to echo inside my head.

hunks.baseline: “You humans… are a real shitshow.”
hunks.sol: *You humans… really are a shitshow.*

hunks.baseline: I never thought I would live to hear something like that from a monster.
hunks.sol: I never thought I’d hear that from a monster.

hunks.baseline: But I couldn’t think of anything to say in response.
hunks.sol: But I had no answer.

hunks.baseline: No—maybe I had simply lost all my strength the moment I saw that picket sign.
hunks.sol: Maybe seeing that sign had taken the fight out of me.

hunks.baseline: Even though I hadn’t used that much internal energy, the mental exhaustion was considerable.

hunks.baseline: I gave the Skeleton King, stored in my Inventory, a brief answer, then pulled out the Magic Scroll I had brought along and tore it.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t used much internal energy, but I was mentally exhausted. After giving the Skeleton King a curt reply inside my Inventory, I pulled out the Magic Scroll I’d brought and tore it.

hunks.baseline: The moment the Teleport Magic activated, its distinctive sensation swept through my entire body.
hunks.sol: The familiar sensation of Teleport Magic swept through me.

hunks.baseline: The scenery around me changed in an instant. As my vision quickly recovered, I saw a familiar face.
hunks.sol: The scenery changed in an instant. As my vision cleared, I saw a familiar face.

hunks.baseline: “You got back quickly. I only heard a little while ago that you were returning.”
hunks.sol: “You’re back early. I only just heard you were on your way.”

hunks.baseline: Song Song’s voice was thick with exhaustion. Dark circles that hadn’t been there before hung beneath her eyes, and she immediately pulled out a handkerchief and held it out to me.
hunks.sol: Exhaustion weighed on Song Song’s voice, and she had dark circles under her eyes that hadn’t been there before. She promptly held out a handkerchief.

hunks.baseline: “Wipe your face first. There’s blood on it.”
hunks.sol: “Wipe your face. You’ve got blood on it.”

hunks.baseline: I looked back and forth between the handkerchief and Song Song, then smacked my lips.
hunks.sol: I looked from the handkerchief to her and smacked my lips.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “I’m asking because I’m curious, but are you saving your Clean Magic to make soup with?”
hunks.sol: “Just curious. Are you saving your Clean Magic to make soup with?”

hunks.baseline: “Do you think Magic works by putting coins into it? You can chug potions to replenish mana, but you can’t replenish mental energy that’s already been spent. I’m already not getting enough sleep these days, so shut up and use the handkerchief.”
hunks.sol: “You think I put a coin in every time I cast a spell? Potions can restore mana, but they can’t restore the mental energy I’ve spent. I’m barely sleeping as it is, so shut up and use the handkerchief.”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: I had nothing to say, since I knew exactly who the main reason for her lack of sleep was.
hunks.sol: I knew who was chiefly responsible for her lack of sleep, so I couldn’t argue.

hunks.baseline: I silently wiped away the blood and handed the handkerchief back. Song Song accepted the dirty cloth and quietly chanted a spell.
hunks.sol: I wiped off the blood and handed it back. Song Song took the dirty handkerchief and quietly cast a spell.

hunks.baseline: *Whooosh.*
hunks.sol: *Whoosh.*

hunks.baseline: The dust and blood vanished in an instant, leaving the handkerchief spotless.
hunks.sol: Dust and blood vanished, leaving the handkerchief spotless.

hunks.baseline: Song Song blinked innocently at me as I stared at her in disbelief.
hunks.sol: I stared at her. She blinked innocently.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: That shameless remark—and the fact that Song Song had clearly planned for this situation—made me snort despite myself.
hunks.sol: At that shameless answer—and the realization that she’d set me up for it—I couldn’t help snorting.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “You’re finally smiling. You looked like you were about to die on TV a little while ago.”
hunks.sol: “There. You’re smiling. You looked miserable on TV.”

hunks.baseline: “I watched the whole thing live. I even heard those insane reporter bastards spouting bullshit.”
hunks.sol: “I saw it live. Heard those fucking reporters talking bullshit, too.”

hunks.baseline: “……Well, I suppose I have to put up with it. If you think about it, I am partly responsible for this whole mess.”
hunks.sol: “…Well, I guess I have to take it. When you get down to it, I bear some responsibility for this mess.”

hunks.baseline: Song Song suddenly furrowed her brow.
hunks.sol: Song Song frowned.

hunks.baseline: “Are you going to spout bullshit too?”
hunks.sol: “Are you going to start talking bullshit too?”

hunks.baseline: “Just when I thought you were getting back to normal, what’s this? If you want to blame yourself that badly, kill those bastards first and then beat yourself up all you want.”
hunks.sol: “I thought you were getting back to normal. What’s with you? If you want to blame yourself that badly, kill those bastards first. Then you can beat yourself up all you like.”

hunks.baseline: That was exactly what I wanted to do.
hunks.sol: Nothing would make me happier.

hunks.baseline: But it wasn’t as though that would be easy. Three days had already passed since our trip to Switzerland, and almost nothing had changed.
hunks.sol: But it wasn’t that easy. Three days had passed since our trip to Switzerland, and little had changed.

hunks.baseline: Magic Johnson’s investigation had yet to produce any results. The Prophet’s whereabouts could not be traced even with every kind of Magic and satellite surveillance. And the Odin Guild, led by Michael Silbert, continued to soar higher by the day.
hunks.sol: Magic Johnson’s investigation had produced no results. Neither magic nor satellite surveillance could find a trace of The Prophet. And Michael Silbert’s Odin Guild kept rising higher by the day.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t blame yourself or worry too much. Other people are working hard too, not just you. Uncle Kkeokjeong in particular was running around like a madman yesterday, saying he was going to fly straight to Paris and cut Michael’s head off.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t blame yourself so much, and don’t worry so much. You’re not the only one working hard. Uncle Kkeokjeong was raising hell yesterday, saying he’d go straight to Paris and cut Michael’s head off.”

hunks.baseline: “That… It’s reassuring to have an entire army on our side, but if he did that, Uncle Kkeokjeong would be the one losing his head.”
hunks.sol: “Well, it’s reassuring to know he’s on our side, but if he did that, Uncle Kkeokjeong would lose his own head.”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah, I told him exactly that.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. That’s exactly what I told him.”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. It’s true. Anyway, he looked a little dejected after hearing it, but he accepted it pretty quickly.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. It’s true. He was a bit dejected, but he came around pretty quickly.”

hunks.baseline: That alone was something to be grateful for.
hunks.sol: Well, I was grateful for that much.

hunks.baseline: Song Song and I walked along, exchanging various bits of conversation.

hunks.baseline: By the time I had finished hearing all the news about my mother and Hayeon, who were staying at the mansion under ironclad security, we arrived at the office where Team Leader Choi was waiting.
hunks.sol: Song Song and I talked as we walked. By the time she’d finished telling me about my mother and Hayeon, who were staying at the mansion under tight security, we had reached Team Leader Choi’s office.

hunks.baseline: “You’re back.”
hunks.sol: “You’re here.”

hunks.baseline: He looked even more exhausted than Song Song. The office, which was always kept neat and orderly, was a mess, and the desk was covered with empty coffee cups.
hunks.sol: He looked even more exhausted than Song Song. His usually immaculate office was a mess, and empty coffee cups covered the desk.

hunks.baseline: “Thank you for your hard work on such a long trip. But…”
hunks.sol: “Thank you for making the long trip. But…”

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi looked back and forth between Song Song and me, then lowered his voice.
hunks.sol: He glanced between us and lowered his voice.

hunks.baseline: “Where is the other person?”
hunks.sol: “Where’s the other one?”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t worry. He came with us.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t worry. He came with me.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m here.”
hunks.sol: *I’m here.*

hunks.baseline: Had I left him cooped up for too long?
hunks.sol: Had I kept him shut away too long? He sounded furious.

hunks.baseline: I took the Skeleton King out of my Inventory, pretending to rummage through the subspace pouch at my waist as I recited the command.
hunks.sol: I pretended to rummage through the subspace pouch at my waist as I took the Skeleton King out of my Inventory.

hunks.baseline: The next moment, a sturdy young white man popped into existence.
hunks.sol: A sturdy young white man popped into view. Song Song muttered, “Wow. Easy birth.”

hunks.baseline: Song Song muttered,

hunks.baseline: “Wow. Smooth delivery.”
“Shut your mouth, beautiful but ill-mannered human female. How dare you compare this body to such a thing…”
hunks.sol: “Shut your mouth, beautiful but ill-mannered human female. How dare you compare me to—”

hunks.baseline: “Thanks. That really brightens my mood.”
hunks.sol: “Thanks. I feel so much better now.”

hunks.baseline: “You damn…”
hunks.sol: “Damn you.”

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King’s face was full of displeasure as he muttered a curse, but there was nothing we could do about it.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King looked thoroughly displeased, but we had no choice.

hunks.baseline: *Even if his identity has already been exposed to some extent, we have to hide him as much as possible.*
hunks.sol: *Even if his identity is partly out in the open, we need to keep him hidden as much as we can.*

hunks.baseline: We had scrubbed his past and identity clean, but the word “perfect” did not exist in this world. Even the Pentagon, known to have the best security in the world, had been breached in the same way.
hunks.sol: We’d given him a new past and identity, but nothing in this world was perfect. Even the Pentagon, supposedly the most secure place on earth, had been breached the same way.

hunks.baseline: Given the circumstances, we had no choice but to limit his exposure as much as possible.
hunks.sol: Under the circumstances, we had to limit his exposure wherever we could.

hunks.baseline: But when I heard Team Leader Choi’s next words, I realized that I had to play the Skeleton King.
hunks.sol: But Team Leader Choi’s next words made me realize we would have to play the Skeleton King card.

hunks.baseline: “Three minutes ago, Tokyo Bay collapsed.”[^2]
hunks.sol: “Three minutes ago, Tokyo Bay collapsed.”

hunks.baseline: [^2]: The Korean wording literally says that Tokyo Bay “collapsed,” preserving the alarming ambiguity of the announcement.
